title: Whispers of the Open Road
story:
The morning sun rose bright and warm over the southern outskirts of San Antonio del Río, casting long golden shadows across the highway shoulder. Beyond the final roadside fruit stands, a steep limestone hill rose dramatically above the valley floor, crested with wild green agave and sun-bleached rock. Looking up at the summit, James realized it offered the perfect vantage point to scout the road ahead. He chittered softly to Nico, pointing toward the high ridge, and together they began their scramble up the worn dirt path.

The climb was an invigorating ascent through cool shade and warm pockets of morning sunlight. Nico darted nimbly over loose gravel and stone ledges, while James swung from sturdy roots and rocky outcrops. At the hilltop summit, the valley unfolded into a sweeping panorama. To the north, the tin roofs of the river port shimmered under the clear sky, the distant noise of trucks softened to a gentle hum. To the south, a wide asphalt highway cut a clean grey ribbon through emerald sugarcane fields, trailing toward a majestic horizon of blue mountain ridges.

Perched on a smooth stone overlooking the expanse, James unstrapped the brass map canister from his side and carefully unrolled the parchment across his lap. Nico planted his front paws firmly on one corner to hold it flat against the mountain breeze. James mapped the river bend they had left behind and traced the long asphalt highway sweeping into the open southern valley, successfully marking the path south on his map and preparing his pack for departure.

He safely tucked his drawing charcoal away, slid the map back into its protective brass tube, and tightened the leather straps across his chest. Standing on the windy outcrop next to his small mouse companion, James felt a quiet rush of wonder at how far they had traveled since leaving Oakhaven. The open highway called to them from below, bright and full of promise, ready for whatever lay beyond the next bend.
location: Limestone lookout hill south of San Antonio del Río
